body:
GitHub issue #322.

## Problem

Recording a confirmed prosecution finding to .adlc/findings.jsonl — the bridge
that keeps P7 fed — is implemented in ONE of five harnesses. In the other four
every finding is reported in prose, fixed, and lost.

Evidence:

- grep -c 'record-finding' over all five harness prosecute docs returns 0,0,0,0,0.
- grep -rl 'recordFinding' plugins/ returns exactly one file:
  plugins/adlc-pi/lib/prosecutor.mjs. pi's prosecutor is PROGRAMMATIC so it
  records automatically; the other four are markdown workflows that fan out
  subagents and write nothing.
- In packages/prosecute/bin/adlc-prosecute.mjs, recordFinding is reachable only
  from the explicit --record-finding subcommand. The gate path
  ('adlc prosecute --input') asserts the phase but does NOT feed the ledger.
- Every entry currently in .adlc/findings.jsonl is pi-authored. A Claude Code
  session (#284/#304/#309/#316) ran two prosecution rounds across five lenses,
  produced ~20 verified findings including two pre-merge regressions, fixed them
  all, and recorded zero. lesson-foundry had nothing to cluster, so the defenses
  that session should have generated were hand-authored instead (#317).

This is the same failure class as #284 and #309 one level up: a mechanism that
reports success while doing nothing. 'gate-manifest record prosecution' records
THAT a gate ran; --record-finding records WHAT it found. Only the second
compounds, and 'no clusters to refine' is indistinguishable from 'nothing has
recurred yet'.

## Required behavior

1. All four markdown prosecute commands document the recording step:

     adlc prosecute --record-finding --file <path> --desc "<plain prose>" \
       --category <lens> --severity <s>

   It belongs at VERIFICATION time — once a finding survives the verifier and
   before it is handed off to be fixed — NOT in the final record+verdict step,
   where a CLEAR verdict means there is nothing left to record.

2. Guidance matches recordFinding's own contract: plain-prose --desc with no
   quoted or backticked literals, so a cluster routes to a spec-gap template
   rather than a lint rule. --file and --desc are required (the recorder fails
   closed without them).

3. A PARITY TEST enumerates the harness prosecute docs FROM DISK and fails if
   any lacks the step, so a sixth harness cannot ship without it. Prose that
   nothing checks is exactly what rotted here. The repo already uses this shape
   (scripts/test/codex-skill-depth-parity.test.mjs, flag-consistency.test.mjs).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Every harness prosecute command documents 'adlc prosecute --record-finding',
   positioned at verification time. Verify by reading each doc.
2. A test discovers the prosecute docs by GLOB (not a hardcoded list) and
   asserts each documents the bridge. Verify: adding a new doc without the step
   reds the test.
3. The test fails if the step is deleted from ANY single doc. Verify by deleting
   it from one and observing red, per doc.
4. The test asserts the discovered set is non-empty, so a glob that matches
   nothing cannot pass vacuously.
5. The documented invocation is valid against the real CLI contract: --file and
   --desc present. Verify against packages/prosecute/bin/adlc-prosecute.mjs.
6. npm run preflight green.

## Constraints

- Do NOT change packages/prosecute or @adlc/core behavior; the recorder works.
  This ticket wires the workflows that never call it.
- pi's programmatic recorder is the reference behavior — do not regress it.
title: Wire the P5 to P7 finding bridge into every harness, not just pi
